branches/branch-1/ledger.jsonl.text: New comparator qualification from primary P code: ada/P-models.py:30-45 constructs the scratch classical CNN with ordinary nn.Conv2d when transfer=False, whereas transfer=True selects FilterNormalizationConv2DParallel. The latter normalises each unfolded input patch in ada/P-modules.py:94-105; the quantum route also normalises patches at :59. Therefore the published ordinary CNN is not the exact input-normalised, circuit-parameter classical comparator identified in entries 4 and 10. Its comparison can confound input normalisation and weight parameterisation with quantum implementation. This does not invalidate the demonstrated instantaneous transfer map, but similar ROC-AUC cannot isolate a quantum training effect. Source: [P model routing](https://github.com/anthonysmaldone/Quantum-to-Classical-Transfer-Learning/blob/474781690264e117960db573c844302ebc1998b6/src/models.py#L30-L45) and [normalised classical convolution](https://github.com/anthonysmaldone/Quantum-to-Classical-Transfer-Learning/blob/474781690264e117960db573c844302ebc1998b6/src/modules.py#L94-L105). No model was run.

branches/branch-2/ledger.jsonl.text: prior-work search dated 7 October 2026 is recorded in emmy/literature-search.md and literature-search-log.json, with 31 verbatim web queries and access failures. Examples: "Quantum-to-Classical" "transfer" "2025" Smaldone; HiMap NetBFE optimal design relative binding free energy variance network; quantum neural networks amplitude encoding data loading complexity inner product classical data. Primary sources: [QKDTI 2025 publisher PDF](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-07303-z.pdf) explicitly cites P as reference 5 but uses quantum kernels/SVR rather than exact learnable-weight transfer. [Quantum-Train](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11304) and [QT-CNN 2025](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11011133) already cover quantum-to-classical parameter generation with classical deployment; direct citation to P was not verified for these. [NetBFE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.04726) already allocates RBFE resources adaptively using measured variance. [HiMap](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10547263/) already explicitly asks in Discussion/Design Weights how noisy weights may be while designs remain efficient. Thus the broad decision-quality/noisy-score question is also prior art, not merely optimal-design integration. [Landman 2022](https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2022-12-22-881/) Section 2.1 counts data-loader preprocessing, gate count and depth; Section 2.2 counts inverse-square precision shots for dense-network inner products. [AMLET](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.13108) addresses loading cost with structured approximate preparation. These cover the components of our frontier; none was verified to establish this particular RBFE compiled-cost curve. No novelty or publication verdict follows from this bounded search.
